test.title: Section 1 · a castle and insulation grants

topic.en: Two everyday texts: visiting a castle and getting a grant to insulate a home.
topic.kk: Екі тұрмыстық мәтін: қамалға қалай баруға болады және үйді жылытуға грант қалай алынады.
topic.ru: Два бытовых текста: как посетить замок и как получить грант на утепление жилья.

paragraphs.text: Dunmore Castle — visiting information. The castle and gardens are open every day from March to October, 10 am to 5 pm, with last admission at 4 pm. From November to February only the gardens and the tearoom are open, and only at weekends. The castle stands on a steep hill, and the walk up from the lower car park takes about fifteen minutes; visitors with limited mobility may be dropped off at the upper gate, where there are four reserved parking spaces.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Tickets bought online are ten per cent cheaper than at the gate and can be used on any day within three months. An adult ticket costs £12, and children under five enter free. Guided tours of the great hall and the kitchens leave from the courtyard at 11 am and 2 pm and are included in the ticket price. The towers can only be visited on a tour, as the staircases are narrow and the number of people inside must be controlled.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Dogs on leads are welcome in the gardens but not inside the castle, except for assistance dogs. Photography is allowed everywhere except in the chapel, where the painted ceiling is sensitive to light. Picnics may be eaten on the lawn below the east wall, and the tearoom serves light lunches until 3 pm. Please note that the castle may close at short notice in high winds, so it is worth checking the website before you set out.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Home insulation grants — Westbridge Council. Householders in the Westbridge area can apply for a grant towards the cost of insulating their lofts and walls or replacing an old boiler. The scheme is open to owners and to tenants, although tenants need written agreement from their landlord before any work begins. Grants cover up to seventy-five per cent of the cost, to a maximum of £4,000 per home, and households with a member over seventy may receive the full cost.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: To apply, complete the short form on the council website or collect a paper copy from any library. An assessor will then visit your home, usually within three weeks, to measure the property and recommend the work that will save the most energy. You will receive a written offer listing the approved work and the amount of the grant, and this offer remains open for ninety days.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Work must be carried out by one of the installers on the council’s approved list, and it must not start before the written offer has been accepted; the council cannot pay for work that has already been done. When the work is complete, the installer sends the invoice directly to the council, and the householder pays only the remaining share. The scheme closes when the money for the year has been spent, so early applications are advised.
paragraphs.label: C
